headline: South Asia: PM Shehbaz reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia in meeting with new envoy
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: PM Shehbaz reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia in meeting with new envoy.
- Western Russia: One killed, five injured and buildings damaged in Russian attacks on Ukraine's west – video.
- Africa: Sudan: Drone Attack Kills Two in North Darfur As Red Crescent Volunteer Killed in Blue Nile.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: What is the US Army doing in Panama? A bit of everything..
- Military Times, 7 hours ago: What is the US Army doing in Panama? A bit of everything..
As Washington shifts its attention toward the Western Hemisphere, a reinvigorated jungle school is just one part of the evolving U.S. presence in Panama.
- Military Times, 3 hours ago: ‘Weaponized light’: KBR’s new base defense technology pits lasers against drones.
The Pentagon recently selected KBR's Firefly system for a pilot program to test defending U.S. military installations against adversarial drones.
- Military Times, 21 hours ago: US Army eyes developing soldier-worn drone detection gear.
The Army is in the early stages of developing and testing a wearable or lightweight device that could alert soldiers to the presence of hostile drones.
The Caribbean - bottom line: 19-y-o charged with Kidd Lane triple murder.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: 19-y-o charged with Kidd Lane triple murder.
A 19-year-old man has been charged with three counts of murder in connection with last Friday’s deadly attack on Kidd Lane, off Spanish Town Road in St Andrew, which claimed the lives of two women and a one-year-old boy. The accused, Dante Davis, who has addresses on Spanish Town Road and Kidd Lane in Kingston 13, is also facing charges of conspiracy to commit murder, arson, conspiracy to commit arson, possession of a prohibited weapon, unauthorised possession of ammunition and using a firearm to commit a felony.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

September civilian casualties in Ukraine rose to 328 killed and 2,105 injured, driven largely by long-range missiles and drones, according to the UN.

Russian strikes ignited massive fires at businesses in Odesa and Zaporizhzhia as President Zelensky met European leaders for talks.

Yemen’s Houthi rebels have struck Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport 20 times since the start of October. A spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition said the attacks involved 10 drones, four ballistic missiles, four cruise missiles and two unidentified projectiles.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: PM Shehbaz reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia in meeting with new envoy.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: PM Shehbaz reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia in meeting with new envoy.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its “sovereignty, security and territorial integrity” amid a recent escalation in Houthi attacks. According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the premier made the remarks during a meeting with newly appointed Saudi Ambassador Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy. He welcomed the envoy to Pakistan and congratulated him on assuming his new responsibilities.
- The Hindu - International, 7 hours ago: Airstrikes, artillery hit north Ethiopia as government and rebels clash, sources say.
Air attacks killed at least 17 people northwest of Tigray’s capital Mekelle — which federal government forces took over the weekend — according to a bulletin circulated among humanitarian groups
- Dawn (Pakistan), 15 hours ago: Trump banking on ‘swift end’ of Iran war to bring down fuel prices.
• Pezeshkian decries US blockade, insists ‘military force’ will not compel Tehran into submission • Washington weighs using ‘Mother Of All Bombs’ against Iranian energy sites, CNN reports WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump once again predicted a swift end to the war with Iran, and a sharp drop in oil prices once the conflict concludes, even as Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian warned that military action cannot force them into submission. “The Iran war will end very soon … Soon, as they want it to end,” Trump told reporters in Montana.
- The Hindu - International, 10 hours ago: Drone strikes in the Black Sea raise fears of Russian escalation to test NATO's response.
The attacks in the two countries' exclusive economic zones threaten a global shipping route and have left two people dead, with at least 25 still missing. They also run the risk of drawing other countries directly into the war for Ukraine
India - bottom line: Zelenskyy slams Trump's diesel deal, says will help fund Putin’s war in Ukraine.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Zelenskyy slams Trump's diesel deal, says will help fund Putin’s war in Ukraine.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has expressed concerns over the US diesel deal with Russia. He warned that this agreement could provide additional funds for Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine. Zelenskyy emphasized the need for Europe to increase support to Ukraine as missile attacks continue. The president requested significant financial assistance to maintain Ukraine's defense against Russian aggression.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: US temple plot, school shooting: Gun epidemic spares no one as debate goes off target.
A neo-Nazi teen attempted a mass shooting at a Hindu temple in Illinois, but his rifle jammed. The attack highlights ongoing debates about gun violence and societal issues, including parenting and mental health. Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi expressed horror that the attack targeted Indian Americans during worship. Many lawmakers condemned the incident, emphasizing the need to address religious and racial hatred in society.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Return of Gulf oil: Has Iran lost grip on Hormuz & what does it mean for India?.
The US war with Iran exposed Tehran’s ability to disrupt the global economy by blocking the Strait of Hormuz. Before the war, around 19 million barrels of crude oil were exported daily from the Middle East. However, September data from tanker-tracking firm Kpler showed oil flows recovering to an average of 16 million barrels per day, the highest since the conflict began.
